text: One golden rule to good health is regular exercise, which can be free of charge, for example running.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Food is not free, but the best and healthiest choice is home-cooked food.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Buying fresh produce and cooking at home is generally cheaper than eating out.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I have come across low-income families who do not cook.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: One common reason is lack of time, because some have more than one jobs to make ends meet.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I especially worry for their kids who might resort to convenience food like instant noodles, which offer little nutrition.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I have also met some seniors who live by themselves in rental flats.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It is too much of a hassle for them to cook for themselves or he could be a widower who does not cook.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: So, I would like MOH to share if it has done some studies on this issue and how it plans to help low-income Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The phrase "prevention is better than cure" is often used to encourage people to adopt preventive health measures in their lives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I commend the Health Promotion Board and other stakeholders who have passionately and persistently engaged Singaporeans to take on preventive health measures at the community and national levels.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As we move forward, I would like to ask how will MOH encourage Singaporeans across all ages to take on preventive health measures, such as doing timely health screening, vaccination and quit smoking?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Healthcare is not one size-fits-all, and often community providers are best able to customise services to fit the needs of local populations or vernacular groups.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Over the years, we have seen many community providers coming forward to play a part and contribute towards a healthier Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These community providers have helped to empower Singaporeans to lead a more active lifestyle and taking ownership of their health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As good health and active lifestyle are expected to continue to be an important national agenda, I would like to know how the Ministry is supporting these community providers, especially during this COVID-19 period?

speaker: Mr Charles Chong
text: Mr Chairman, the speaker before has already said all the things that I wanted to say.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong
text: So, I shall not repeat them, other than to say that I support what Assoc Prof Dr Faishal Ibrahim has said.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Chairman, as the Minister for Health has shared, we have delivered on our Healthcare 2020 objectives, including having Minister Gan remain as the Health Minister till now.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Today, Singaporeans live longer, healthier lives than when we made these goals in 2012.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We enjoy some of the best healthcare in the world, and this remains affordable and also accessible to all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But the future will bring new challenges, and we cannot afford to rest on our laurels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It will take bold steps – from Government and the community in partnership – to ensure that we can continue keeping these commitments to our citizens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our healthcare financing system has weathered the test of time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Each financing scheme plays a unique role in ensuring that no Singaporean will be denied appropriate care because of an inability to pay.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: First, Singaporeans enjoy means-tested subsidies across public healthcare settings, covering up to 80% of the costs of treatment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Singaporeans are also covered by MediShield Life for large hospitalisation bills and costly outpatient treatments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Coverage starts from the moment one is born, and is for life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Next, MediSave helps Singaporeans set aside some income towards future healthcare needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It can be used to offset out-of-pocket expenses and also pay for health insurance premiums.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Seven in 10 subsidised hospitalisations by Singaporeans do not incur any out-of-pocket expenses or payment, while eight in 10 incur payments of less than $100.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Still, we regularly review each pillar of healthcare financing to give Singaporeans peace of mind in seeking the care they need.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As our population ages, we can expect more Singaporeans to face chronic conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling asked how we are supporting chronic disease patients, and Dr Chia Shi-Lu asked specifically about what we can do to encourage them to seek early intervention in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We also expanded CDMP to cover ischaemic heart disease and pre-diabetes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Today, CDMP covers 20 conditions, including four mental health conditions: schizophrenia, major depression, bipolar disorder and anxiety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We regularly review the list of CDMP conditions in consultation with clinical experts, and will include conditions such as eczema in our review.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Last November, we introduced higher subsidies for complex chronic conditions for CHAS Blue and CHAS Orange card-holders, and also expanded CHAS Orange to cover common illnesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We also launched the CHAS Green card – part of a wider initiative to shift healthcare beyond hospitals and into the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: All Singaporeans are now eligible for subsidised CDMP treatments at CHAS GP clinics, regardless of income levels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This represents a fundamental shift in primary care financing, with universal subsidies for GP treatment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Ms Irene Quay asked for an update on the success of these measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: With our continuing efforts to bring more clinics onto the scheme, CHAS card-holders can now receive subsidised treatment at close to 2,000 GP and dental clinics island-wide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This year, we will be further expanding the use of MediSave for CDMP treatments in outpatient settings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Currently, Singaporeans can tap on the MediSave500 scheme for CDMP treatments, for approved vaccinations and screenings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: From 2021, we will increase support for patients with complex chronic conditions by raising their annual withdrawal limit from $500 to $700.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Patients with complex chronic conditions include those who have visits for two or more CDMP conditions, or one CDMP condition with complications, within a year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is aligned with the higher CHAS subsidies we implemented for complex chronic patients in November.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In effect, rather than MediSave500, these patients will in fact benefit from an extension of the scheme, or MediSave700.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Administratively, we will align MediSave500 with all other MediSave schemes, shifting from a per-account to a per-patient limit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling asked us to consider greater flexibility in the MediSave withdrawal limits, especially for seniors with significant balances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I believe Mr Pritam Singh also raised the same issue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have been working to increase flexibility under MediSave in a few key areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are expanding MediSave to cover severe disability under the upcoming MediSave for Long-Term Care scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: With cash withdrawals, patients will also have greater flexibility to choose appropriate care options, relevant for themselves and their particular circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, first we cover new schemes and new treatments, and second, we look at increasing flexibility within the scheme itself.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: One example is lowering the age threshold for Flexi-MediSave in 2018 from 65 to 60.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Another example is the MediSave700 scheme I have just outlined.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The higher withdrawal limits increase flexibility for patients with complex chronic conditions, as they are likely to incur higher costs for their CDMP treatments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu asked how we can plan to keep healthcare affordable for elderly Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The three pillars of our long-term care financing framework – CareShield Life, MediSave Withdrawals for Long-Term Care, and ElderFund – mirror the "3M" schemes that we have for acute care, and that has worked well for us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They complement existing subsidies of up to 80% for long-term care services, such as day care and home care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: CareShield Life provides better protection for severely disabled policyholders with lifetime payouts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: MediSave Withdrawals for Long-Term Care, or MediSave Care for short, will allow Singaporeans to withdraw directly from their MediSave in cash, providing flexibility for long-term care expenses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh asked how we are supporting families who might fall outside of the subsidy thresholds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, we have those within the framework, that I have just outlined.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: What happens to those who might fall outside the subsidy thresholds?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: First, let me clarify that the current income criterion of $2,800 for long-term care subsidies covers close to two-thirds of resident households in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The median household income per member quoted by Assoc Prof Goh includes the employer CPF contributions, which we exclude in assessing the eligibility for subsidies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The figure is also based on all employed households, and does not consider households with no working persons.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Elderly households, or households with elderly members, tend to have a lower income per household member.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Hence, a larger proportion of such households will qualify for subsidies, with many qualifying for the maximum rate of subsidies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Together with CareShield Life and other schemes highlighted by Assoc Prof Goh, most Singaporeans will be adequately covered for basic long-term care needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In addition, as I mentioned to the House last year, we will allow private insurers to introduce additional severe disability coverage on top of CareShield Life, with premiums payable from MediSave.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Faisal Manap asked if patients with physical impairments can obtain support from MediFund for transportation costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is an area where new measures complement the existing schemes to provide multiple layers of support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We provide means-tested subsidies of up to 80% for patients requiring transport for centre-based services, dialysis or medical appointments at polyclinics and also at SOCs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Patients who need additional assistance may tap on cash payouts under ElderFund or other schemes, to defray the costs of travel to and from medical appointments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, we look at the overall framework and these are the schemes that sit outside that supplement and work with the existing framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Financial concerns represent only some of the challenges that Singaporeans face when loved ones encounter disease or disability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Beyond being able to afford care, we want Singaporeans to feel supported in caring for each other as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Ms Yip Pin Xiu has asked about our long-term plans for eldercare.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Over the years, we have improved the accessibility of aged care services and also deepened the range of services and options available in the community and residential care settings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Last year, for instance, we launched the Care-giver Support Action Plan to support those caring for seniors on their care-giving journeys.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Since then, we have been working with the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) and various community partners to roll out new initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Some initiatives focus on care navigation and care-giver training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Care-givers can obtain information and access referral services at four new AIC Links touchpoints in Toa Payoh, Nee Soon, Pasir Ris and also Choa Chu Kang, which complement the eight existing touchpoints already existing in our heartlands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have also worked with healthcare professionals to introduce a course on the "ABCs of Care-giving", with customised components to help care-givers with the different mobility needs of their loved ones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Within the eldercare landscape, there is a range of care-giving options.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Many families engage foreign domestic workers (FDWs) to provide care and Ms Yip Pin Xiu asked if care-giver training initiatives will be extended to them as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: There are, indeed. merits to training FDWs and families can decide on how best equip them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have initiatives to support those who choose formal training for their FDWs, such as the Eldercarer FDW Scheme which we have run since 2016.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Training is done before placements in the households that they serve and includes both classroom theory and as well as on-the-job practical training in managing the day-to-day care-giving needs of an elderly person.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza has asked about our measures to provide respite care and how effective they have been.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have recently expanded the range of respite care options as well, starting with a respite care pilot in September 2019 for care-givers of cancer patients on home palliative care and a night respite care pilot in December 2019 for care-givers of persons with dementia, who experience behavioural and sleep issues at night.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And sometimes, these difficulties cause the care-giver not to have his or her own rest.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have also been helping care-givers access respite care at short notice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Care-givers under our Go Respite pilot launched in April last year were able to pre-enrol for these services and activate the respite care at short notice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Allow me to share the story of one care-giver, to illustrate how our schemes address the care-givers' different types of needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Shahril lives with his wife, three children and a 79-year-old father, who is bed-bound after a stroke and heart attack.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In October 2019, Mr Shahril needed a break from care-giving duties, as his helper had left the country for home leave.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: He shared this with the AIC Link staff at Changi General Hospital where his father was treated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Within two weeks, they enrolled Mr Shahril's father in AIC's Go Respite programme at the NTUC Health Nursing Home, across the road from their home, across the road from where they live, and he began his three-week stay there.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This arrangement made it easier for Mr Shahril to continue to provide for his own family, with the assurance that, at the same time, his own father was being cared for during this period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At the same time, Mr Shahril also applied for the Home Care-giving Grant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Today, his family receives a monthly payout of $200, which they use for essential items, such as diapers, milk supplements and other disposables, as well as for his father's medical expenses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: All in all, our schemes have given Mr Shahril the flexibility and the assurance to care for his father in the long term.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I have shared how the Ministry is taking important steps to help address the cost of care, both financially and otherwise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These will support Singaporeans in seeking the necessary care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But at the same time, we must take bold steps to encourage healthier lifestyles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I think Members have heard that narrative from the speakers before me.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This will delay the onset of disease and reap downstream savings for our healthcare system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Members will also be, nonetheless, familiar with our efforts on this front.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Minister had previously described some of our efforts to promote healthy living under the war on diabetes initiative.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Although we have made progress in encouraging Singaporeans to exercise more and eat healthier, our daily sugar intake, as some Members have pointed out, remains high.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In particular, beverages contribute to more than half of the sugar intake.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Both Mr Charles Chong and Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked for an update on our plans to control the consumption of such beverages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The same issues and questions have been raised by Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar in the House last week, while Mr Leon Perera also made suggestions what else we could do should these measures not prove to be effective.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As a start, let me outline what we will do.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, two elements – sugar and saturated fat.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We want to provide Singaporeans with the right information to make their own healthy choices and also, at the same time, encourage the manufacturers to reformulate their products and create healthier options, a point that Mr Perera also raised.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Under this new regulatory framework, all pre-packaged beverages will be given a colour-coded nutrient-summary label, called the ‘"Nutri-Grade".

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This provides a quick, at-a-glance summary of the nutritional quality of the beverage, allowing consumers to compare across products at the point of purchase.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example, beverages with more than 5% sugar content will be graded C, while beverages with more than 10% sugar content will be graded D.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But beverages may subsequently be "downgraded", at the point in time, be downgraded to D, if they also contain a high amount of saturated fat.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We encourage all manufacturers to label their products with the Nutri-Grade, but the label will only be mandatory for beverages in Grades C and D.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The label is intended to facilitate Singaporeans' decisions when they go and purchase these products at the point of purchase.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It will therefore not only be displayed on the front of product packaging, but also at points-of-sale the where customers do not have direct access to the product.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example, at e-commerce websites, vending machines, drink fountains, they will be displayed at the point-of-sale as well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This will reduce the impact of advertising on consumer preferences and encourage manufacturers to reformulate.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will continue to allow advertising of Grade A to C beverages, as well as all brand advertising, as we want to encourage manufacturers to reformulate.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The point is not to deprive Singaporeans of their favourite drinks, but to encourage manufacturers on their journey towards reformulation to create a wider and broader range of healthier options for Singaporeans to enjoy.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The new regulations will be published at the end of 2020, coming into effect a year later.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If manufacturers start today, they will have almost two years to reformulate their products in line with these regulations and avoid being in groups, Grade C or D where they have to compulsorily put on the label.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Health Promotion Board (HPB) will continue to support industry reformulation efforts through initiatives such as the Healthier Ingredient Development Scheme.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And HPB will also launch a campaign to educate consumers on using the Nutri-Grade labels to guide purchase and consumption decisions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: At the same time, we have heard strong calls from all quarters to also regulate – beyond just the pre-packaged – the freshly prepared beverages, such as herbal drinks and bubble teas.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is clear that they are a substantial and growing source of sugar intake for many Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar, in particular, asked whether there are plans to extend our regulations to these drinks.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Over the past few months, I have met representatives from the freshly prepared beverage sector to hear their views on how we can work with them as well to help consumers make that transition to healthier choices.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Most understand the need to inform consumers about the nutritional quality of their products and they support our objective of reducing Singaporeans' overall sugar intake.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As a start, these measures will apply only to the larger chains, which are more likely to have consistent recipes, as well as significant reach and impact locally.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will study the local landscape to determine the appropriate criteria for what comprises a "large chain".

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Other jurisdictions with mandatory labelling in F&B settings have, in their own countries, adopted thresholds of 10 to 20 outlets as being the definition of "large chain".

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But we will study this in our own context.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will take reference from what has been done in other countries, which means that small businesses with one or two stalls, such as those in hawker centres, would not be affected in the first instance.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Nevertheless, we will monitor the impact of these measures, and may gradually seek to extend them to more establishments – along the vein of what Mr Perera had mentioned earlier.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Concurrently, we encourage F&B outlets not considered "large chains" to voluntarily adopt these measures.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will continue to engage the industry in the coming months to finalise details of these measures, including how to implement them in a cost-effective manner.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: More details will be shared when they are ready.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: All these initiatives are part of a longer term approach to reshape consumer behaviour towards healthier living, not just in the choices that they make, but in consumption.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Some have suggested stronger measures, such as an excise duty or an outright ban.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These will require further study, like those suggestions that Mr Perera raised.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In the meantime, we will work closely with industry partners to support Singaporeans in making those healthier choices.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, on that front, we have been working with agencies like NEA, HDB, LTA and also NParks to increase the availability and accessibility of drinking water in the community.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Water dispensers are available in 30 hawker centres – Members might be pleased to know – and are also easily found in parks across Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In addition, 14 bus interchanges and terminals already have water coolers and we will work with LTA and public transport operators to install water points in bus and MRT stations where suitable.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In mid-2020, HPB will launch a nation-wide campaign to promote plain water, as part of their nutrition literacy campaign.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Whether you are exercising in our public parks, enjoying a meal at the hawker centres, taking a bus, about to take a bus, or in the MRT station, we encourage you to choose plain water and we will make the options available as much as possible.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Better health for us all is a vision and responsibility we must all share.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We urge Singaporeans to partner with us as we strive for a healthier Singapore not only in 2020 but beyond.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Beyond Healthcare to Health – going upstream and supporting healthy living.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: To push this transformation, we will do three things which I will cover in my speech.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: On better financial support, we want Singaporeans, regardless of income or social background, to enjoy good health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will do so in a fiscally sustainable, targeted and effective manner.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: (b)	Second, subsidies for nationally recommended adult vaccinations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: (c)	Third, subsidies for nicotine replacement therapies for eligible participants at smoking cessation pilots.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Today, only recommended childhood vaccinations against infectious diseases with high outbreak potential such as measles and diphtheria receive full subsidies, and this is only available at polyclinics in the primary care setting.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: There are currently no subsidies for adult vaccinations and smoking cessation in the primary care setting.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Full subsidies will be given to Singaporean children for all vaccinations recommended under the National Childhood Immunisation Schedule or NCIS.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Subsidies will be available at polyclinics and at CHAS GP clinics across Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: For Singaporean children up to the age of six, full subsidies for child developmental screenings will be extended from polyclinics to include CHAS GP clinics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We are doing this to ensure early detection and timely intervention for developmental delays for all Singaporean children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This measure is part of our ongoing efforts to ensure Singapore remains one of the best places to raise a child.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: So I urge parents to take advantage of the free vaccinations to give our children the best possible start.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: All eligible Singaporean adults will enjoy subsidies for vaccinations under the National Adult Immunisation Schedule or NAIS at polyclinics and CHAS GP clinics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The NAIS covers seven types of vaccines that protect against 11 diseases, including influenza and pneumococcal disease.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: NAIS recommends vaccination to two main groups of adults: The first group, persons with certain medical conditions such as diabetes, chronic heart diseases and chronic respiratory diseases; and the second group, seniors aged 65 and above.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This corresponds to CHAS Blue and Orange cardholders at CHAS GP clinics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Other eligible Singaporeans will get 50% subsidy for the vaccinations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Pioneer Generation get an extra 50% subsidies and Merdeka Generation get an extra 25%, off the remaining co-payment amount.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Now Singaporeans pay about $70 to $80 for PPSV23 pneumococcal vaccination at a polyclinic.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Assuming you fall within the NAIS recommendations and qualify for the subsidies, you can expect to pay about $20 to $40, depending on means-test.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Singaporeans can continue to pay out-of-pocket amounts using MediSave.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Singaporean adults will receive similar levels of means-tested subsidies for these vaccinations at CHAS GP clinics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: To ensure vaccination subsidies are passed to eligible Singaporeans at CHAS GP clinics, MOH will introduce fee caps for NAIS and NCIS vaccinations done at CHAS GP clinics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: MOH have also worked with vaccine manufacturers so CHAS GP clinics can get these vaccines at favourable prices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We are studying ways to help those who may have difficulties going to polyclinics and CHAS GPs, such as nursing home residents, to benefit from these subsidies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I mentioned earlier about providing the subsidies in a fiscally, sustainable and targeted, effective manner.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: First, the NAIS scopes the group of people whom the Expert Committee on Immunisation (ECI) has assessed to be more vulnerable to certain diseases and are therefore recommended for the vaccinations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Second, our aim is to reduce the number of people who fall ill from vaccine-preventable diseases.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Singaporeans with chronic medical conditions are particularly vulnerable and fall sick more easily.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: If diseases can be prevented, we can gain system-wide savings in the long run.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Essentially, this is what we are doing: keep out vaccine-preventable diseases through vaccinations, keep our people out of hospitals and keep them healthy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Perera asked about the coverage of childhood vaccinations and how we can raise adult vaccination coverage in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Coverage for childhood vaccinations in Singapore is high, with most vaccinations exceeding 95% coverage in the past five years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This is due to efforts in health promotion, comprehensive childhood immunisation services and a robust school health service.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: All childcare centres and kindergartens require immunisation certifications for compulsory vaccinations under NCIS before enrolment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Parental inertia and lack of awareness are some of the reasons a small minority of children are not vaccinated.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We have a two-pronged approach to increase children and adult vaccinations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The first is to make vaccinations affordable through subsidies and the second, public education.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Subsidies will be given for nicotine replacement therapy, if found suitable, in smoking cessation pilots.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Singaporeans can benefit from intensive behavioural support, follow-up for up to a year and a 3-month nicotine replacement therapy, if found to be suitable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We plan to start the pilots after Public Healthcare Institutions (PHIs) resume normal operations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This will depend on how the COVID-19 situation develops.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Charles Chong asked about existing measures to assist smokers to quit and their efficacy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Smoking is one of the biggest risk factors for poor health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Standardised packaging for tobacco products will start in July 2020.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The minimum legal age for smoking will be raised to 21 next year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This will set a good momentum to drive down our smoking rates further.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I shared in 2018 our stretched target of reducing our smoking rate to below 10% by 2020.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will do our best to reach that stretched target.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: SPS Faishal asked about community health promotion activities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Indeed, cultural connections and understanding are strengths we are tapping on to mobilise the community towards a healthy cause.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: HPB's Jaga Kesihatan, Jaga Ummah (JKJU), which means take care of health, take care of community is one good example.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: JKJU brought together MUIS, 28 mosques and Malay Activity Executive Committees.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I am proud that they have reached out to over 35,000 Malay participants in 2019.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This is important, involving the community and powering community institutions to take ownership and mobilise people to action.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Masjid Maarof organised piloxing, zumba, a skit on coping with dementia and urged congregants to give up a cigarette puff for a less calorie curry-puff ("A Puff for a Puff").

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Masjid Al-Ansar offered circuit training and stretch-band exercises for seniors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We are stretching out to involve more partners and people.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Our Regional Health Systems (RHSes) will partner JKJU to bring more quality programmes and deepen outreach.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This will help greatly, it is a promising partnership.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Because RHSes treat patients who are residents in the area, they know the local ailments and the common problems within the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: RHSes can help local partners like JKJU shape programmes, provide targeted interventions customised to local needs and offer medical expertise to raise awareness on community trending topics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I am also proud of the excellent work of Chinese and Indian community groups, 27 churches and 10 temples have worked hard to organise health promotion programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: From health screenings, national step challenge roadshows to physical activity workouts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Hindu Endowment Board, SINDA and Narpani and various places of worship partnered HPB and reached out to 5,000 people in 2019.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Hindu Endowment Board partnered National Healthcare Group to conduct health screenings for 1,500 people at Sri Perumal Temple in 2019.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng asked about helping lower income Singaporeans stay healthy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: HPB will pilot the "Healthy Living Passport" in mid-2020, beginning with five sites located in Boon Lay, Woodlands, Jurong Spring, Chua Chu Kang and MacPherson.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We aim to reach at least 15,000 residents, about 5,000 families, over a three-year period.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Healthy Living Passport seeks to improve health literacy and promote healthy lifestyles, customised to the needs of lower income residents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: They shared with us about working shifts, not having enough sleep and missing out on various community exercise programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: They shared that healthier food such as vitamins, vegetables and low-calorie options tend to be more expensive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: They raised stress as a concern and many, unfortunately, turned to smoking to unwind.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We should try to address them and hear them out.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Healthy Living Passport is a modest effort, a sincere outreach to help our fellow Singaporeans lead healthy lives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We are still working out the exact parameters of Healthy Living Passport.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Broadly, we are focusing on equipping participants with knowledge on shopping for budget, healthier ingredients and prepare healthier, tasty meals and promote physical activity, oral health and mental wellness.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We are targeting to impart health tips to both parents and children in a fun and interactive way.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Volunteers from HealthySG Buddies will encourage and support families to use this Healthy Living Passport and embark on a meaningful and fulfilling journey.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Charles Chong asked how MOH empowers and supports community care providers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We are committed to supporting community partners deliver better care to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: An example is the Tote Board Community Healthcare Fund.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This fund helps non-profit organisations pilot and scale innovative projects in preventive health and community care.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Tote Board Community Healthcare Fund funds the Wellness Support Package.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This package supports nursing homes to upskill their manpower and implement senior-friendly activities such as table-top gardening and wheelchair taichi.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Seniors enjoy these activities and homes reported improvement in seniors' mood, well-being and self-esteem.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: For instance, the RHS-HPB Integrated Volunteer Network and the Shared RHS-HPB Learning Hub.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We recruit, train and deploy HPB Health Ambassadors and RHS volunteers together to promote health in the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: In 2020, we aim to bring volunteers from all public hospitals on board the Integrated Volunteer Network.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Advances in technology present opportunities to better tailor programmes and messages, and engage residents and deliver effective programmes to the right person, at the right time, at the right place.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: In the next few years, HPB will develop a Population Health Data Hub.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This will be a national data hub containing information such as demographics, lifestyle and health information.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Hub will help us better understand Singaporeans’ lifestyle, behaviour and health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Interventions and nudges may be customised to individual’s needs and lifestyle, empowering behavioural change and driving health outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This will help us to better address the causes of ill health early, and reduce incidence of chronic diseases.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We are developing a virtual Health Booklet (vHB) that can send personal reminders, empowering individuals to better manage health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We expect to launch the virtual Health Booklet in end-2020.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We are making good progress with HPB’s National Steps Challenge.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Now in its fifth season, more than 850,000 participants have taken part.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Participants have grown more active with more step counts and higher intensity physical activity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Under Screen For Life, over 62,000 individuals aged 40 years and above have gone for cardiovascular screening at CHAS GP clinics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Of those with borderline and abnormal screening results, 84.4% have gone for medical follow-up as at 9 January 2020.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We want more Singaporeans to attend screening and follow up on their screening to reduce risk of developing chronic diseases.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This year, we will pilot tele-coaching for people found to be at risk of cardiovascular diseases through the Screen for Life programme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: HPB's health coaches will reach out to selected individuals and invite participants to work on health goals through HPB or other programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: (In Malay):   Please allow me to put on record our highest appreciation to our frontline officers battling against COVID-19 and I would like to give a reminder on the importance of staying healthy through two poems.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This first poem is an ode to our healthcare workers who are the heroes that we admire and respect.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The second poem is a reminder to everyone to wash their hands with soap and to practise this good habit daily.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Regardless of income or background, we want all Singaporeans to enjoy good health and a good quality of life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: These subsidies will be available at all polyclinics and CHAS clinics in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Full subsidies will also be provided for childhood developmental screenings for Singaporean children aged six and below, at all polyclinics and CHAS clinics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Early detection and recovery will result in better outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: To quote a Malay proverb – bend a bamboo while it is still a bamboo shoot.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We want our children to start their lives healthy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This is an on-going effort to ensure Singapore remains one of the best places to raise children and have a family.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This subsidy will be given for vaccinations recommended under the National Adult Immunisation Schedule (NAIS) for some groups of adult Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: First, seniors aged 65 and above; and second, those with chronic medical conditions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: NAIS covers seven types of vaccines that protect against 11 diseases, including influenza and pneumococcal disease.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: In general, these are the CHAS Blue and Orange cardholders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Pioneer Generation receives an additional 50% subsidy while the Merdeka Generation receives an additional 25% off the remaining co-payment amount.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I urge all Singaporeans, especially parents and seniors, to take advantage of this subsidy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Singaporeans can continue to pay out-of-pocket amounts using Medisave.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: For instance, the pneumococcal vaccination (PPSV23) now costs about $70 to $80 at polyclinics for seniors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: With the subsidies, Singaporean seniors pay only about $20 to $40.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: It is even lesser for the Pioneer and Merdeka Generation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Singaporean adults will receive similar subsidies if they go to CHAS clinics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Third, subsidies for nicotine replacement therapies for those undergoing smoking cessation therapies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will commence the smoking cessation pilot programme in public healthcare institutions after the COVID-19 situation subsides and normal operations resume.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This programme will target 10,000 smokers and will offer counselling, nicotine replacement therapy if suitable and follow-up consultations up to a year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Do not wait until it is too late.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Do not wait until you fall ill to quit smoking.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: These include the "Kita Dah Cukup Manis" campaign to reduce sugar consumption, the "Puff for a Puff" programme to quit smoking, and the "Get Fit for Haj/Umrah" and "Move and Be Happy" programmes to invite everyone to be more active.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I am heartened and confident that there is a noticeable change.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: When I was out for Hari Raya visits, I was often served plain water and reminded that "We are already sweet enough, aren't we?" Yes, definitely sweet enough.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Let us enhance our efforts together to stay healthy and have a sweeter life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Let us support one another to stay healthy.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: I just have two clarifications for Senior Minister of State Lam and two for Senior Minister of State Edwin Tong.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: For Senior Minister of State Lam, besides building new polyclinics, are there any plans to redevelop or refresh existing polyclinics, given that many of the polyclinics are growing long in the tooth.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: I may have missed his answer but I was wondering whether there are any plans to improve the system or to strengthen the system.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: For Senior Minister of State Edwin Tong, I think I am very heartened to hear about this new Nutri-Grade labeling system.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: But I saw on the slide that the label was "subject to change".

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: I was just wondering whether Ministry has tried it out or done some test-bedding of these labels to see how effective they are, how clear they are.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: And my second question is, I note that he said that 70% of these pre-packaged drinks would be classified as C or D.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: I was wondering of that percentage, how many are actually under D.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Of course, we will review and look at the requirements on the ground and for those polyclinics that can be redeveloped to cater to the increased capacity, we will do so.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As for PHPC, currently, we do not have plans to enhance it.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We feel that with the current 800 to 900 PHPC clinics on the ground, in fact, it is serving its purpose well but having said that, I think we will see how the COVID-19 situation evolves.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: If need be, we can enhance it as and when necessary.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On Dr Chia's two questions, the Nutri-Grade label, yes, it is subject to change as we look at the design.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But he will be heartened to note that we have already looked at it very closely.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We had about 12 focus group discussions and also studied with the food science people, people who looked at it from a behaviourial perspective.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In fact, after this we will be putting up on our website the report of the findings that we have gathered from these focus group discussions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And so, generally, the label is designed, having in mind simplicity, giving fullest of information in terms of the choice, but also easy to recognise so that those who are not so conversant, the elderly, may be able to distinguish them.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Looking at these numbers, you can see why we have said earlier that there is a strong desire for us to encourage the market to reformulate on their own.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Because much as you design the Grading system, what we also want to ensure – and we do not ban the items – so what we want to ensure is that the market, on its own, corrects it, and – I think, it is a point that Mr Perera made – manufacturers do appreciate that the market is looking out for healthier options.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This is one of the ways, along with the advertising ban, that we want to push market in a particular direction.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On the Member's final point about the soda fountains, yes, I mentioned that to the extent that we are not able to have the consumers review the product grading – the Nutri-Grade – before it is actually purchased, then at the point of sale, in other words, perhaps at the cashier or at the place where the orders are taken, that summary label will also be available.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo
text: And will MOH be able to cope with this?

speaker: Dr Lily Neo
text: And whether does our Government have more specific measures in place to cope with this scenario?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Dr Lily Neo for this very important question.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As I mentioned in my speech, we do expect to see more cases coming in, given the emerging cases all around the world.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Many countries are beginning to see confirmed cases of COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have raised precautionary measures: as you have seen, in recent days.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have introduced new travel advisories as well restrictions and we have also introduced a swab practices for those passengers or travellers who are showing signs of being unwell.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: These will help us to prevent or to minimise the number of imported cases.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But some of these cases may still be imported because it is not possible to stop every case.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Many of them may enter without symptoms because it is still within the incubation period.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They may begin to fall sick while they are in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, it is important for us to re-emphasise the need for us to pay attention to public health and personal hygiene.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: That is why I mentioned that the SG Clean campaign is very important.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Through this campaign, we hope to build a strong foundation of public health, raise the standard of public health – whether it is in our food outlets, in our public areas, in our public toilets – and at the same time, also entrench a higher standard of personal hygiene, and look at how we can improve some of the social practices like common servicing spoons and chopsticks in our restaurants.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: These will go a long way in helping us to minimise and reduce the risk of widespread community transmission.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As of today, we still do not have evidence of widespread transmission in our community here, but we cannot allow our guard to come down.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have to continue to be mindful and to exercise and practise high levels of personal hygiene.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching
text: Senior Minister of State Lam shared about this national antimicrobial surveillance report.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching
text: I just wanted to ask if the results are ready and how are we faring in terms of our antibiotic utilisation in the community?

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching
text: What are our national targets and what are we doing about it?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, I would not be able to let Ms Irene Quay know what the initial results are.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The report will be released for public viewing.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: I have got two clarifications for Senior Minister of State Amy Khor.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Earlier, she mentioned the Community Care Nursing Leadership Programme, or CCNLP.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Though the Senior Minister of State shared that the Government is rolling out assisted living flats to expand housing options for seniors, I still wonder whether there will be enough assisted living flats for all seniors, especially with an ageing population.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to the Member's first question about the Community Nursing Scholarship and how this relates to the Community Care Nursing Leadership Programme.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Community Nursing Scholarship is for fresh school leavers, whether they are "A" Level or existing nursing students.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: What we are doing is trying to inject fresh talent into the community care sector – those with leadership potential and who have a passion to serve in the community care sector.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As the Member has said, that started in 2017.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Although, of course, the class sizes in the Polytechnics are bigger, but those under this scholarship programme, there are 17 now.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For the Community Care Nursing Leadership Programme, this is a talent development programme.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is leadership development for the existing cohorts who are already registered nurses.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They do not have to be in the community care sector.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, any registered nurse with good, strong clinical skills as well as nursing experience, and who are interested to join the sector, could apply for this.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They will have an individual development plan for them to become leaders, take leadership positions in the sector.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Regarding assisted living, the Member's question was whether there will be enough.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: One of them, of course, would be 2-room flexi flats.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They can also choose to stay in their existing flat and get the Home Improvement Programme (HIP) and the Enhancement for Active Seniors (EASE), and then, get services like home care, day care and so on, and with the support of family.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is really to meet different preferences, needs as well as lifestyle aspirations.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This might be useful for a group of seniors who want to be independent, live independently, may not have very strong family support, who feel that as they get more frail, they will need more services.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition, they want to prevent themselves from being socially isolated, they want to have some kind of communal living and yet have some privacy.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, that is what this assisted living housing form is for.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will monitor the demand and decide if we will build more of this housing form.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said, we are also looking at a pilot in the private housing market.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: I first want to thank Senior Minister of State Amy Khor for announcing to the House that there will be a whole-of-Government and multi-Ministry effort to address mental health as a national priority.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: It is very sweet, D grade-worthy news, I think.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: But I hope that it is not just the elderly and the youths that we are looking at, because the sandwiched ones are the very ones who are playing a big role in the mental well-being of our youths, and they are also the care-givers of our elderly.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: So, if the Senior Minister of State will indulge me, I have four clarifications and one comment, from the four cuts.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: I understand the Ministry is not intending to bring to parity the limits for MediSave and MediShield in terms of physical and mental health conditions, which, to me, would be the loudest anti-stigma signal, with that parity.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Can I urge MOH to conduct its own public consultation or studies to examine the many affordability issues that were raised in our own rudimentary public study that I shared both in the Budget debate speech and earlier.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: I know because I think we all understand that the treatment process for mental health conditions is a lot —

speaker: The Chairman
