speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I think it is more like six follow-up questions, not four.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First of all, this thing about parity between MediSave and MediShield Life.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have tried to explain, when we set the withdrawal limits for MediSave or MediShield – say, inpatient, for the different types of treatment, different types of conditions, not just mental health but other conditions, we look at the bill sizes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But for acute hospital, the average bill size, taking out the cost of surgery procedures, is $480.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And as I have said earlier, for inpatient MediSave withdrawal limit, less than one in 10 actually exceed their $5,000 yearly withdrawal limit and less than three in 10 exceed their daily limit.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is not the absolute amount but what is the bill size.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I assure the Member that we will and we have always continued to monitor to make sure that the withdrawal limits are adequate, to make access to healthcare affordable to our subsidised patients.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And, as I have said for MediShield Life, the MediShield Life Council is reviewing the MediShield Life limits for the different conditions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, the same thing with MediSave withdrawal for outpatient treatment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, if a doctor says under anxiety, it is OCD, it is covered.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I only listed a few, because I did not have enough time.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For wait time, as in for access to many other treatments, we are always mindful of the wait time.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: What we are doing to try and reduce the wait time is that for the hospitals and polyclinics, they are trying to see how they can review their work processes to optimise the appointment slots.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, you try to tighten the triaging, so, they call the patient before the appointment, to try and optimise these slots.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are also looking at tiering of services to provide the appropriate level of care, because not everything has to go to the specialists.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: When it is possible to get care in the community or in primary care sector, then we will refer them to the primary care sector or community care sector.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If they do not need to go to a specialist, they can be treated or cared for in the primary care sector.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And, actually, there is no wait time, and they still can get a subsidy, through CHAS as well as through CDMP.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If they access care through the community intervention teams, the first referral is within two weeks – 14 days – a lot shorter.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: That is what we are trying to do.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And then, only for the more complex cases, they go to the specialist – to try and shorten the wait time.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Besides that, if urgent medical mental health assistance is needed or they need to see the doctor immediately, they can contact IMH through the 24-hour Mental Health Helpline or show up at the IMH 24-hour Emergency Services.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Having said that, we are working on how we can reduce the wait time.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, I hope that answers the Member's question.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Regarding mental health of the LGBT community, as I have said earlier, healthcare providers who are caring for all persons with mental health conditions, are trained and they are supposed to provide these patients with empathy, sensitivity and due consideration to their specific care needs as well as risk factors.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: What we have done is to adopt a team-based approach to healthcare and ensure that different perspectives are considered.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If need be, they can get the experts to come in to provide holistic care.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This clinic provides counselling and psychiatric treatment for persons experiencing emotional difficulties pertaining to gender identity, including the people who are diagnosed with gender dysphoria.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And approximately 50% of these patients have a co-morbid psychiatric diagnosis.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Majority of them will have anxiety and depressive disorders, and they are actually treated there.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, there are various avenues that we help this group of people.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I think I have answered all the queries.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If the community care provider is working together, say, with the GP or with the polyclinic and they are referred to them, then I think they can access MediSave.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But, of course, the community care provider must be qualified.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Besides raising the retirement and re-employment age ahead of schedule, what else is MOH planning to do to support older healthcare workers and maximise their employment at the workplace?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: My second question is for Senior Minister of State Lam.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: He announced the introduction of the Integrated Youth Service in Woodlands with Care Corner.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Could the Senior Minister of State share more details about what services are provided under this Integrated Youth Service?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The public healthcare institutions welcome older workers or mid-careerists to work in the public healthcare sector.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, we are doing everything we can to attract as well as to retain our mid-careerists and to re-employ older workers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Some of the things that we have done is firstly, to design age-friendly workplaces as well as put in place age-friendly employment measures.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, redesigning the job roles, flexible work arrangements, part-time, for instance.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The nurses now have access to part-time work, more flexible work arrangements, as well as even preparing, what we call, pre-retirement preparatory training to prepare them to be re-employed again or to encourage them to be re-employed again.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And then, in the community care sector, we are also working to redesign jobs so that they can be broken up and seniors or older workers can do part-time work.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They break up care roles so that seniors could be escorts to bring the patients to the senior care centre or care for them through active ageing programmes in a care centre.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Another one would be to reduce the manual burden or workload on the senior workers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, patient uplifters, transfer aids and so on, which are really helpful to our healthcare workers, including nurses.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: There are basically four services that IYS provide.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: First, which is to outreach for prevention which is to increase awareness and encourage help-seeking behaviours.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This is done through activities like roadshows, talks and workshops on mental health topics.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The second service they provide is to identify needs and to provide a one-stop service for care coordination.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The third service will be for peer facilitation and mentoring.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, at IYS, we will look for model youths who will provide that kind of a role model for these youths at-risk as well as to look for youth volunteers who can actually better engaged these youth during activities like roadshows and outreach programme.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And the last service that IYS provides is to provide emotional support and monitoring.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: It can be done in the form of group sessions to improve resilience as well as coping skills.
